analysis:
Reviewed scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py (head lines 1-874 supplied). The change is an offline CI self-test: it adds assertions that the provider-test-gate's record step calls `ci-tested-tree.py tree-name --tree --components` (head lines 393-394), adds the 'Upload the tree record' step to the conditional list, and changes the build-job `if` expectation so build jobs run only when `inputs.<lane> == 'true'`. It also drops the push-of-tested-tree cache-refresh build condition. The patch excerpt is truncated after the build-job `if` change, so the remainder (lines 886-900 on head) was not visible to me.

Security-relevant observations: the file is a test, not production code, and introduces no runtime attack surface for provider keys, attestation, or the coordinator/provider WebSocket boundary. No threat-model assets (A-001 to A-020), boundaries (TB-002 to TB-014) or threats are weakened by these edits. The test retains guards that matter for CI integrity: pinned action SHAs, the cache steps gated by SAVE_CACHES (pull requests never save caches), the validated restored `.git` (no symlinks, hooks, or fsmonitor/include config), verified-only prompt fixture caching keyed on manifests, and the provider-test-gate requiring every lane even after failures. The T-041 prefix-cache definition is unrelated to these changes.

Remaining integration questions: the corresponding provider-plan.yml, ci-tested-tree.py (tree-name subcommand) and provider-tests.yml changes are in other units and need review. In particular, how the 'tree record' is named and uploaded, and whether skipping build jobs on a push of a tested tree can be bypassed or can let a tree be marked tested without running tests. The weakened-looking test expectation (build jobs no longer run on push-skip) should be matched against the real workflow so that gate coverage is not silently dropped.
